author: ramanuja
summary: Ramanuja's commentary on the Bhagavad Gita, reading it as teaching devotion to a personal God, supported by knowledge and action.
whyRead: This commentary shows how the Gita reads when bhakti, not knowledge alone, is taken to be its culmination. It is central to the Sri Vaishnava tradition and a natural counterpart to Shankara's commentary.
questions: Is devotion the Gita's final teaching?
How do knowledge, action and devotion relate?

keyTeachings.title: Bhakti as the goal
keyTeachings.text: Knowledge and action are treated as disciplines that lead to and support devotion, which is the direct means to God.

keyTeachings.title: Self-knowledge as a step
keyTeachings.text: Knowing the self as distinct from the body is an important step, but not the end; the self is then known as belonging to God.

keyTeachings.title: Surrender
keyTeachings.text: His comments on the Gita's closing teaching became important for the Sri Vaishnava theology of refuge (prapatti).

passages.about: The call to take refuge in Krishna

relatedTexts.note: A modern commentary that also gives surrender a central place
